newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 15.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's Daily Variety:
* Warner Bros spokesmen were working overtime Monday responding to a letter from the White House protesting the use of President Clinton's image in the movie "Contact."

* In the biggest TV affiliate switch since News Corp's Fox snagged the New World stations in 1994, the WB TV Network has agreed to pay the Sinclair Broadcast Group $84 million over 10 years for converting five of its stations from UPN to WB affiliates.

* Lawyers for Sony Pictures Entertainment and John Travolta are expected to ask the Los Angeles Superior Court for a six-month continuance Tuesday on their lawsuit for "The Double," in order to try and reach an out-of-court settlement.
* "Hercules" is on track to become Walt Disney 's least-successful animated feature in eight years.

* Director Martin Scorsese is near a deal to reteam with screenwriter Paul Schrader on "Bringing Out the Dead," a novel by Joseph Connelly about a burned-out Gotham-based paramedic. * Hoping to revive the charming young doctor that inspired a generation of medical dramas, the Paramount-based Cort-Madden company and Gotham-based Boardwalk Entertainment have teamed to produce a big screen update of "Dr. Kildare."
